case_context.index_subject_description: 36-year-old pregnant woman at 11 weeks of gestation with new-onset hyperthyroidism diagnosed as Graves’ disease after alemtuzumab treatment for multiple sclerosis

evidence.quote: A 36-year-old woman in the 11th week of her first pregnancy was referred to our Unit for new onset of hyperthyroidism.
A 36-year-old woman
Patient’s Age | 36 years old
A 36-year-old woman
The patient delivered a baby girl weighing 3610g
The patient had a history of multiple sclerosis, diagnosed at the age of 27
referred to our Unit for new onset of hyperthyroidism
diagnosed with GD at 11 weeks of gestation, 16 months after receiving her last ALZ dose
Based on clinical and biochemical findings, a diagnosis of GD was rendered
GD Onset | First trimester (11 weeks)
ALZ Interval | 16 months post-ALZ
the patient developed GD 16 months after receiving her third course of ALZ
During pregnancy regular obstetric US showed normal fetal growth and no signs of fetal hyperthyroidism.
Fetal Thyrotoxicosis | None (serial US normal)
At 10 days of life, thyroid function tests indicated neonatal hyperthyroidism
The infant experienced transient neonatal hyperthyroidism with spontaneous recovery without treatment.
Neonatal Thyrotoxicosis | Delayed onset at day 10, requiring hospitalization

Currently, at seven months postpartum, the patient is euthyroid on 15 mg/day of MMI (Table 1) and shows no clinical or radiological signs of MS relapse, with postpartum MRI and follow-up confirming disease stability.
with no clinical/radiological signs of multiple sclerosis relapse
At presentation she reported fine distal tremors of the upper extremities.
The patient showed no signs of active ophthalmopathy.
Her thyroid US, physical examination, electrocardiography, and growth rate were all normal.
